did_you_know.text: Did you know? In Ezekiel’s vision, water flows out from under the threshold of the temple and runs eastward, from the right side of the temple, near the altar area.
Did you know? The man measures the stream in sections of a thousand cubits; at first, the water reaches his ankles.
Did you know? As the measuring continues, the stream becomes deeper: first the water reaches the knees, and then the waist.
Did you know? After another measurement, the stream becomes so deep and full of water that it cannot be crossed by swimming or wading.
Did you know? The water brings life wherever it flows: living creatures multiply in it, and there are very many fish.
Did you know? Along the stream, from En Gedi to En Eglaim, fishermen stand and spread their nets; the fish there are described as extremely abundant, like the fish of the Great Sea.
Did you know? Despite the blessing brought by the water, the marshes and pools remain unhealed and are left for salt.
Did you know? Fruit trees grow on both banks of the stream, producing fruit every month, and their leaves are for healing; their water comes from the temple.
Did you know? In the future division of the land among the twelve tribes of Israel, the tribe of Joseph receives two portions, as Ezekiel says: “Joseph—two portions.”

Did you know? The vision of the division of the land also includes the foreigners living among the Israelites: they will receive an inheritance within the tribe where they reside, as citizens of Israel.
